items.title: Friends of the liver: Punjab’s quiet epidemic of male heartbreak
items.summary: In Punjab, a pair of lifelong best friends are called jigri yaar : friends joined not merely at the heart but at the liver. The phrase suggests an intimacy so deep it is almost anatomical, as if friendship has passed beyond feeling and entered the body. Punjabi songs and Hindi films have long celebrated this kind of male devotion: two men eating from the same plate, sleeping under the same quilt, risking death for each other, calling each other brother because no other word is available. What these stories rarely make room for is what happens when one of those men leaves. For those of us who came of age in the 1990s, before terms like gay, lesbian, and bisexual entered our vocabulary, these portrayals of fraternal love provided rare openings. They allowed us to expand our suppressed desires into the realm of fantasy. Queer philosopher Judith Butler has argued that fantasy is not the opposite of reality but rather shaped by it, filling in what reality so frequently denies. For queer men like me, such fantasies created possibilities beyond what was immediately available. items.title: Advocates and court staff perform essential duties: Delhi HC says while exempting them from non-BS VI vehicle ban
items.summary: The government has failed to explain how non-BS VI vehicles have suddenly become a major contributor to pollution, the Delhi High Court observed while exempting lawyers and court staff working in Delhi courts from the ban. Justice Amit Mahajan noted that these vehicles were allowed in the capital till last month. "The respondents have also not been able to point out, at this stage, how the same vehicles which were though not contributing to the pollution till the month of October, are suddenly being considered as a major contributor to the pollution," the Court observed. It added that advocates and court staff perform essential duties. "Once the Courts are functional, the Advocates and the Court staff’s attendance is, undoubtedly, of utmost importance for the smooth functioning of the Court and they cannot be directed to not ply their vehicles. It is not the case of the respondents that they have been providing adequate transport to the Advocates and the Court staff for coming to the Courts," Justice Mahajan said.
